chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Salama ibn Hafsh, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

The Zakat al-Fitr is due on every small and large person, free or slave, for every person one supports (meaning: upon whom one spends), a sa' of dates, or a sa' of barley, or a sa' of raisins. Then, when the time of Uthman came, he changed it to two mudds of wheat.

key_terms.صَدَقَةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (the alms of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: What are the original and later forms of Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar establishes the baseline obligation of Zakat al-Fitr as one sa' of staple food for every dependent, reflecting the Prophet's original practice. It highlights a significant jurisprudential development during the caliphate of Uthman, who substituted the measure with two mudds of wheat, a change often cited by Shia scholars to discuss the flexibility of the specific commodity while maintaining the value of the obligation. This narration underscores the practical application of fiqh in adapting religious duties to changing economic and agricultural contexts.
